title: Resolved version
description: The one record of which GraphCompose build a workspace's work is against. Written by scripts/preflight.mjs at the start of a run and read by every step that would otherwise resolve the version again for itself. Three files used to answer this question — the host build file, flow.config.json and the project's targetGraphComposeVersion — and nothing compared them; one run carried 2.2.0 in the manifest and 2.2.1-SNAPSHOT in the project for its whole ninety minutes.

resolvedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the resolution. Stale by design: it says when the build behind the pin was last looked at, which is what makes a re-resolution meaningful.

version.description: The pinned version, verbatim, SNAPSHOT suffix included. A snapshot is not its release and is never recorded as one.

buildFile.description: Which build file the pin was read out of. Recorded because a walk-up can reach a file the reader did not expect.

build.description: What the pin resolves to in the local Maven repository — the output of describeArtifact(). `identifiesOneBuild` is the fact everything downstream branches on.

origin.description: local-install: someone's `mvn install` put it there, so it exists on no other machine.

supersededBy.description: Releases already installed past a SNAPSHOT pin. A non-empty list means the pin sits behind its own line.

pins.description: Every place a version was found, and whether they agreed, as of the last preflight.

accepted.description: A person was shown a pin that names no single build and chose it anyway. Bound to the jar it was given for: same name with different bits reopens the question, which is the point of asking it about a mutable build.

decision.description: Which build this is and why it is the right one to measure against. An acceptance with no reason is the silence the record replaces.
